findings.evidence: `instance : CoeSort (IntegralLattice V) (Type u) := ⟨fun L ↦ L.carrier⟩` (IntegralLattice/Basic.lean:82); grep for `instance.*Module ℤ` under TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice returns no matches; pre-PR `orthogonalSumCarrierEquiv ... := prodCarrierEquiv L M` typechecked at exactly `↥(L.carrier.prod M.carrier) ≃ₗ[ℤ] L × M`.
findings.fix: Delete the second paragraph (and preferably define the equiv as `Submodule.prodEquiv L.carrier M.carrier`, as the pre-PR code effectively did).
findings.issue: The added paragraph claims this equiv targets "the canonical integer-module structures on the lattice carrier types rather than the module structures inherited from their ambient submodules". No such separate structure exists: `↥L` unfolds to `↥L.carrier` and its `Module ℤ` instance is the submodule one, so this is definitionally `Submodule.prodEquiv L.carrier M.carrier`.

findings.evidence: `@[to_additive prodEquiv ...] def prodEquiv (s : Submonoid M) (t : Submonoid N) : s.prod t ≃* s × t` — mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Submonoid/Operations.lean:506, giving `AddSubmonoid.prodEquiv` for `AddCommMonoid`s.
findings.fix: Cite `AddSubmonoid.prodEquiv` as the additive analogue and drop the "does not apply" clause; keep only the true content (this is the `≃ₗ[R]` refinement of the additive equivalence).
findings.issue: Docstring says this is "the module refinement of `AddSubgroup.prodEquiv`" stated "over an arbitrary semiring and additive commutative monoids, where that additive-group statement does not apply". The additive analogue at exactly this generality exists and does apply, so the stated generality gain is wrong.

findings.evidence: `private noncomputable def quotientProdMap` (Quotient/Prod.lean:41); `quotientProdEquiv := LinearEquiv.ofBijective (quotientProdMap p q) ...` (line 69).
findings.fix: Drop the second paragraph, or replace it with a pointer to the usable interface: `quotientProdEquiv_apply_mk` / `quotientProdEquiv_symm_apply_mk`.
findings.issue: The `quotientProdEquiv` docstring documents the construction ("built directly from `Submodule.mkQ` and `Submodule.liftQ`, so its computation rules remain in the submodule quotient API") rather than the object, and the referenced construction is unavailable to readers: `quotientProdMap` is `private` and the definition is `LinearEquiv.ofBijective`, so no consumer can use those defeqs.

summary: Two new docstrings state rationales that are factually wrong: the lattice carrier equivalence claims a module-structure distinction from Submodule.prodEquiv that does not exist, and Submodule.prodEquiv cites AddSubgroup.prodEquiv while claiming no additive statement applies at monoid generality, when AddSubmonoid.prodEquiv does.
